title: Subject → verb → object
explanation: A basic statement names the person doing the action first, followed by the action and its object.

examples.meaning: I drink water.

title: Identity with 是
explanation: 是 connects the subject to a noun describing their identity or category. Here, it says that I am a student.

examples.meaning: I am a student.

title: Questions with 吗
explanation: Adding 吗 to the end of a statement turns it into a yes-or-no question. The basic word order stays the same.

examples.meaning: Are you a teacher?

title: Negation before the verb
explanation: For this habitual action, 不 goes directly before the verb 喝. It changes “drink” into “do not drink”.

examples.meaning: I do not drink tea.

title: Location with 在
explanation: Here, 在 describes where someone is. Use 在 followed by the name of the place.

examples.meaning: He is at school.

title: Time before the verb
explanation: 今天 gives the time and goes before the action 学习. 今天我学习汉语 is also accepted: the time expression can go before or after the subject.

examples.meaning: I study Chinese today.

title: The object after 喜欢
explanation: 喜欢 means to like something. The thing you like follows the verb; 中国菜 is a single phrase here.

examples.meaning: I like Chinese food.

title: Number → classifier → noun
explanation: When counting books, put the classifier 本 between the number 三 and the noun 书. 三本书 means three books.

examples.meaning: She has three books.

title: Time and destination
explanation: 明天 places the action tomorrow. 北京 follows 去 as the destination. 明天我们去北京 is also accepted.

examples.meaning: We are going to Beijing tomorrow.

title: 也 before the verb
explanation: 也 means “also” and goes before the verb 喜欢. The comma separates two simple clauses. The two 茶 tiles and the two 喜欢 tiles are interchangeable.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢茶，爸爸也喜欢茶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chá, bàba yě xǐhuan chá.
examples.meaning: I like tea, and Dad likes tea too.

title: Written tones and connected speech
explanation:
In Mandarin, pitch patterns help distinguish words. Pinyin marks the four tones: mā (high and level), má (rising), mǎ (low, with a possible rise), and mà (falling). These are a guide to pitch, not four different volume levels.

A third tone is often low without a full dip and rise inside a phrase. When two third tones meet, the first is usually pronounced like a second tone: 你好 is written nǐ hǎo but commonly spoken ní hǎo.

A neutral-tone syllable is short and unstressed; its pitch depends on the preceding tone. These questions check tone concepts. They do not measure your spoken pronunciation or acoustic tone accuracy.

examples.meaning: Mum — first tone: high and level.
Tea — second tone: rising.
Water — third tone; its shape depends on context.
Be — fourth tone: falling.
Mum — the second syllable is neutral in this common pronunciation.

title: Introducing a name with 叫
explanation: 我 means “I” and 你 means “you”. Use 叫 for a name: 我叫安娜 means “My name is Anna”. Use 是 before a noun describing an identity: 我是学生 means “I am a student”.

examples.meaning: My name is Anna.

title: Possession with 的
explanation: 爸爸 means “dad” and 妈妈 means “mum”. 我的妈妈 means “my mum”: the owner comes first, then 的, then the person or thing. With close family, 的 is also often omitted, as in 我妈妈.

examples.meaning: My mum.

title: Wanting to do something with 想
explanation: 喝 means “drink”. Start with the subject, then the verb, then the drink: 我喝水. 想 before the verb expresses wanting to do something: 我想喝茶 means “I would like to drink tea”.

examples.meaning: I would like to drink tea.

title: 从 … 到 …
explanation: 从 introduces the starting point and 到 the destination. Place the route before the question 怎么走 to ask how to get there.

examples.hanzi: 从这儿到火车站怎么走？
examples.pinyin: Cóng zhèr dào huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.meaning: How do I get from here to the railway station?

examples.pinyin: Cóng xuéxiào dào shāngdiàn hěn jìn.
examples.meaning: It is close from the school to the shop.

title: 要 + action
explanation: 要 before an action can express an intention. A time word such as 明天 comes before the action; 一起 means doing something together.

examples.hanzi: 明天我要和朋友一起去旅游。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ yào hé péngyou yìqǐ qù lǚyóu.
examples.meaning: Tomorrow I am going travelling with a friend.
We are watching a film together tomorrow.

title: verb + 了
explanation: 了 after a verb can mark a completed event. A time expression supplies the time reference; 了 is not a general past-tense ending.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.
examples.meaning: Yesterday I bought a book.
I have already eaten breakfast.

title: A 比 B + adjective
explanation: 比 introduces the comparison standard. The adjective follows both items. Do not add 很 simply to turn the comparison into an adjective sentence.

examples.meaning: Today is colder than yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū bǐ nà běn shū piányi.
examples.meaning: This book is cheaper than that book.

title: 请 + person + action
explanation: 请 introduces a polite request. 帮 means help, and 一下 can make a short request sound less abrupt. The request still needs an action or context.

examples.meaning: Please give me a hand.
Can you help me?

title: Routes, plans and comparisons
explanation: Combine a time expression with a plan, then use 从 and 到 for a route. A comparison with 比 helps explain a choice. This checkpoint reuses the patterns of this path.

examples.hanzi: 明天我们一起去火车站。
examples.meaning: Tomorrow we are going to the railway station together.
Taking the bus is faster than walking.

title: verb + 过
explanation: 过 after a verb describes an experience at an unspecified time. It differs from simply narrating one completed event with 了. A negative experience uses 没有 + verb + 过.

examples.meaning: I have been to Beijing.

examples.hanzi: 我没有参加过这个活动。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu cānjiā guo zhège huódòng.
examples.meaning: I have never taken part in this activity.

title: 正在 + action
explanation: 正在 marks an action in progress at the reference time. The activity follows it directly. It does not by itself say that the action is finished.

examples.meaning: He is preparing for an exam.

examples.hanzi: 我们正在讨论这个问题。
examples.meaning: We are discussing this question.

title: verb + result complement
explanation: A result complement follows the action and says what it achieved. 听懂 means listen and understand; 看完 means read or watch to the end. 了 can mark completion of that result.

examples.meaning: I understood this story after listening to it.

examples.pinyin: Tā kànwán le nà běn shū.
examples.meaning: She finished reading that book.

title: subject + 把 + object + action/result
explanation: 把 places a specific affected object before the action. These examples include the result or direction of the action, rather than ending with a bare action verb.

examples.meaning: Please close the door.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ fángjiān dǎsǎo gānjìng le.
examples.meaning: I cleaned the room.

title: 因为 … 所以 … / 虽然 … 但是 …
explanation: 因为 gives a reason and 所以 its consequence. 虽然 introduces a fact that contrasts with the result expressed by 但是. The two patterns express different relations.

examples.hanzi: 因为下雨，所以我们在家学习。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒmen zài jiā xuéxí.
examples.meaning: Because it is raining, we are studying at home.

examples.hanzi: 虽然很累，但是我很高兴。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì wǒ hěn gāoxìng.
examples.meaning: Although I am tired, I am happy.

title: Experience, result and explanation
explanation: Connect an earlier experience with a concrete result. Use an explicit reason or contrast to explain what happened rather than placing unrelated sentences next to each other.

examples.hanzi: 我参加过这个活动，所以有一些经验。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cānjiā guo zhège huódòng, suǒyǐ yǒu yìxiē jīngyàn.
examples.meaning: I have taken part in this activity, so I have some experience.

examples.hanzi: 虽然问题很难，但是我们解决了。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán wèntí hěn nán, dànshì wǒmen jiějué le.
examples.meaning: Although the problem was difficult, we solved it.

title: 尽管 … 仍然 …
explanation: 尽管 introduces a concession: an acknowledged difficulty does not prevent the main outcome. 仍然 emphasizes that the situation or action continues despite that obstacle.

examples.hanzi: 尽管存在困难，我们仍然坚持这个决定。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn cúnzài kùnnan, wǒmen réngrán jiānchí zhège juédìng.
examples.meaning: Despite the difficulties, we still stand by this decision.

examples.hanzi: 尽管资源有限，我们仍然取得了进步。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn zīyuán yǒuxiàn, wǒmen réngrán qǔdé le jìnbù.
examples.meaning: Despite limited resources, we still made progress.

title: 既然 … 就 …
explanation: 既然 introduces an accepted premise and 就 connects it to a consequent decision or recommendation. It is useful when the speaker treats the first clause as common ground.

examples.hanzi: 既然大家都同意，我们就开始吧。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán dàjiā dōu tóngyì, wǒmen jiù kāishǐ ba.
examples.meaning: Since everyone agrees, let us begin.

examples.hanzi: 既然目标已经明确，我们就采取行动。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán mùbiāo yǐjīng míngquè, wǒmen jiù cǎiqǔ xíngdòng.
examples.meaning: Since the goal is clear, we will take action.

title: 与其 … 不如 …
explanation: 与其 presents an option the speaker considers less useful, and 不如 introduces the preferred alternative. Keep the two actions or propositions comparable.

examples.hanzi: 与其抱怨，不如采取行动。
examples.meaning: Rather than complain, it is better to take action.

examples.hanzi: 与其浪费时间，不如认真准备。
examples.pinyin: Yǔqí làngfèi shíjiān, bùrú rènzhēn zhǔnbèi.
examples.meaning: Rather than waste time, it is better to prepare carefully.

title: 不仅 … 而且 …
explanation: 不仅 and 而且 connect an initial point with a further point. Here, both benefits belong to the same policy, so the subject stays before 不仅.

examples.hanzi: 这项政策不仅提高了效率，而且减少了浪费。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè bùjǐn tígāo le xiàolǜ, érqiě jiǎnshǎo le làngfèi.
examples.meaning: This policy improves efficiency and also reduces waste.

examples.hanzi: 这个方案不仅合理，而且容易实施。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāng’àn bùjǐn hélǐ, érqiě róngyì shíshī.
examples.meaning: This plan is not only reasonable but also easy to implement.

title: 无论 … 都 …
explanation: 无论 introduces a range of possible conditions, often with a question word. 都 states the outcome that stays the same across those conditions.

examples.hanzi: 无论遇到什么困难，我们都不会放弃。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn yùdào shénme kùnnan, wǒmen dōu bú huì fàngqì.
examples.meaning: Whatever difficulties we encounter, we will not give up.

examples.hanzi: 无论结果如何，我们都承担责任。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn jiéguǒ rúhé, wǒmen dōu chéngdān zérèn.
examples.meaning: Whatever the result, we will accept responsibility.

title: 之所以 … 是因为 …
explanation: 之所以 introduces the claim whose reason is explained, and 是因为 gives the explanation. Use evidence and a clear causal relation; the pattern itself does not make an argument valid.

examples.hanzi: 我之所以支持这个方案，是因为它更合理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhī suǒyǐ zhīchí zhège fāng’àn, shì yīnwèi tā gèng hélǐ.
examples.meaning: The reason I support this plan is that it is more reasonable.

examples.hanzi: 我们之所以改变计划，是因为发现了新的证据。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhī suǒyǐ gǎibiàn jìhuà, shì yīnwèi fāxiàn le xīn de zhèngjù.
examples.meaning: We changed the plan because we found new evidence.
